text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- ASEAN calls for immediate ceasefire in fighting between rival factions in Cambodia and says its foreign ministers would hold a special meeting in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday to review situation in country "in all its aspects".
- It was not a coup but move to enforce law, close adviser to Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen says in describing military action against rival Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
- Government to introduce new laws to support electronic commerce on Internet, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says.
- Private banker Kevin Wallace arrested in Hongkong following complaints in Singapore and Hongkong from his ex-employer Merrill Lynch.
- Businessman Peter Tay acquitted of retaining stolen property relating to Amcol Holdings Mauritius project.
- Those hoping for tax cuts in Friday's budget reminded that Singapore's current rates score very highly internationally for encouraging individual work initiative and entrepreneurial activity.
- Philippine central bank's Monetary Board is meeting to take up proposal to devalue peso, Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista tells Straits Times.
- Surge in demand for U.S. electronic components and upbeat prognosis for Singapore's non-oil domestic exports sparks interest in electronics stocks in Singapore.

- Wall Street stocks recover from Monday's late-session declines to rally strongly in noon trade on Tuesday. Giving impetus to rise was strengthening of technology sector and optimism for upcoming earnings reporting period.
- NatSteel Ltd wholly-owned subsidiary Eastern Industries will pay Finnish partner Singapore $52.2 million to buy over latter's 45 percent stake in joint venture company Eastern Partek.

- Indonesian-controlled infrastructure company Van Der Horst surges on the stock market in line with general market upturn and talk major shareholder Johannes Kotjo may be looking to raise his stake following forced sale of his shares by banks.
- Heshe Holdings will buy 61.54 percent stake in Jacob's Larder, the operator of Country Manna restaurant chain, for S$1.68 million.
- Another prime site in Stevens Road area will soon be up for grabs -- property group Lim Kah Ngam has decided to sell Equatorial Hotel by tender.
- Lum Chang, Comfort and SBS subsidiary Waterbank Properties sign joint venture agreement to form Boon Lay Executive Condominiums.
